title: The Ring of Gyges
summary: In Plato's Republic, Glaucon tells of Gyges, a shepherd who finds a gold ring in a bronze horse inside a chasm opened by an earthquake. Turning the ring makes him invisible; he uses it to seduce the queen, kill the king and take the throne. Glaucon's challenge: give a just person and an unjust person each such a ring, and they would behave the same way, because people are just only because they fear being caught. The rest of the Republic is Socrates' answer: that being just is good for the person who is just, even if nobody ever sees.
